text:
incident-bot: Pager — severity: P1. Multiple TP4 jobs reporting NCCL timeouts and CUDA Xid 79 on node gpux-42; auto-eviction triggered. Investigate.

oncall-ben: I’m on it. hitting the bridge now. reassigning to carol-sre if escalates.

carol-sre: Joining. quick summary from metrics: across the cluster we see a spike in collective latency and repeated communicator resets starting ~4612349900. Node gpux-42 shows repeated Xid 79 and container restarts.

sam-eng: Noted. recent deploy? I don't see a prod deploy at that time. last config change was autoscaler tweak two hours earlier.

oncall-ben: Logs from the affected trainer container:
```
[2026-03-15T12:25:14Z] NCCL WARN  ->  Timeout waiting for all processes
[2026-03-15T12:25:14Z] Error: ncclCommAbort on rank 2
[2026-03-15T12:25:14Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=12345: GPU page fault
```

carol-sre: Looks like a hardware-facing CUDA fault causing the communicator to abort. Need to cordon node and failover those TP4 pipelines to single-GPU variant.

dave-ml: For the affected jobs, fallback to tp->dp (pipeline->data-parallel single-GPU) reduces perf but keeps customer workloads flowing. We have compatible single-GPU checkpoints for these models.

oncall-ben: Action list: 1) cordon gpux-42 2) drain running TP jobs off node 3) flip routing to single-GPU model variant 4) monitor error rate and customer impact. I'll start cordon now.

oncall-ben: `kubectl cordon gpux-42` -> succeeded.

oncall-ben: Draining non-critical pods; TP jobs marked critical, scheduling drain with graceful window 120s.

carol-sre: I’m triggering automated routing fallback (route policy: prefer-availability -> single-gpu-compat) for the model family foo/large. Will also bump concurrency limits down to reduce chance of OOM.

ops-note-bot: Routing policy updated: foo/large -> single-gpu-compat (canary=true)

eve-support: Heads up: two customers (acct-zen & acct-omni) reporting increased latency and a few 5xx errors since ~12:25. Support has opened tickets; tagging them with incident id INC-4612349999.

dave-ml: Customer impact estimate: peak affected requests ~1.8% of hosted inference traffic for foo/large; latency p95 increased from 180ms -> 720ms for falling-back requests. No data exfil or model mismatch detected.

carol-sre: We saw one container crash with OOM before the Xid79s—likely secondary. Workload memory footprint was near the quantization threshold; starting a conservative eviction of jobs with large seq_len.

oncall-ben: After routing flip, error rate dropped from ~28% to ~3% across those routes. Still seeing intermittent Xid79s on gpux-42 node even after cordon (some kubelet daemons left). I'll force-delete remaining pods.

sam-eng: Running `nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS` on gpux-42 shows ECC corrected errors increasing and repeated GPU resets. Recommend full node drain + reprovision.

carol-sre: Agreed. Marking gpux-42 for reprovision and replacing with spare node. Starting replacement: `kops recreate-node gpux-42 && kubelet restart`.

incident-bot: Handoff to infra team for node replacement. New assigned oncall: infra-oncall.

oncall-ben: Leaving handoff notes: root cause likely intermittent GPU memory corruption (hardware) causing CUDA Xid79 -> NCCL communicator abort -> TP collective hang. Mitigations performed: cordon, drain, routing fallback to single-GPU variants, concurrency reduction, forced pod restarts. Customer impact: 2 known accounts, transient latency increase, small fraction of requests failed briefly.

carol-sre: Post-mortem immediate items: (1) Add auto-fallback earlier in routing policy when NCCL thresholds exceed 10% in 1m window. (2) Add health probe that treats repeated Xid79 as node-unhealthy and auto-cordon. (3) Expand canary coverage for foo/large single-gpu variant to reduce blast radius.

dave-ml: Also add a prompt to model onboarding docs to verify single-gpu checkpoint compatibility and memory headroom testing for pipeline parallel workloads.

eve-support: I'll update customer tickets with mitigation summary and ETA for full resolution (node replacement in progress, expected 25-40m).

sam-eng: Node reprovision kicked off. I'll validate no other nodes show ECC trend. Running cluster scan now.

oncall-ben: Closing immediate page. Keeping thread open for post-mortem notes and timeline. :thumbsup:

carol-sre: TL;DR for post-mortem: hardware GPU fault (ECC/Xid79) cascaded to NCCL communicator aborts during TP pipeline, causing multi-GPU hangs and container crashes. Quick mitigations preserved most traffic by routing fallback; infra replacing node.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident ID: INC-4612349999."
